description: US-37 Past distributions are traceable — the overview and the detail view. THREE BATCHES HAVE MADE A DISTRIBUTION SESSION SOMETHING THE SOFTWARE KNOWS — started and ended by hand (US-34), its hand-outs belonging to it (US-34), the households it served captured as they stood when it closed (US-35) — AND NONE OF IT IS VISIBLE ANYWHERE. DF cannot open last Thursday. This batch is the two screens that make a past session readable: an OVERVIEW at /ausgabetermine listing sessions newest first (Datum, Gruppe(n), Haushalte, Summe, the running one at the top and marked), and a DETAIL VIEW at /ausgabetermine/[id] listing the households that collected, with Nr., Name, Karte, Gruppe, Erw. + Kinder, Preis, Nachweis bis, Erinnerungen and the amount paid. TWO DECISIONS SHAPE THE DETAIL VIEW AND BOTH ARE DF'S. FIRST, IT SHOWS WHO WAS THERE AND NOTHING ELSE: NOT the households that did not turn up (the table of those present is enough) and NOT a list of the blocks and archivings carried out during the afternoon — a block is a property of the household, not a transaction of the session, and is fully readable on the household's own record. That DELIBERATELY SUPERSEDES the passage of the source specification naming „Erinnerungen, Sperrungen, …" in the detail view. SECOND, IT SHOWS THE STATE AS IT STOOD: the name the household had that afternoon, the counts that were true then, the number and card they held, the certificate date on file — and where a session is still RUNNING or has been REOPENED the same screen shows today's live values, because nothing is frozen until the afternoon is closed. ONE SCREEN, TWO SOURCES, AND THE RULE DECIDING WHICH IS ONE LINE IN ONE USE CASE (story 2): is this session ended? If that decision leaks into a component, the screen shows frozen names in one column and live ones in another — the table nobody can check. NINE COLUMNS IS THE RISK: the customer list already has width trouble with eight of them, so whether they all stay readable side by side is DECIDED ON THE FINISHED SCREEN, at DF's window size, and if one has to go KARTE GOES FIRST (a card number is made of the customer number and an issue count, so it partly repeats the first column). NO SCHEMA CHANGE AND NO NEW DOMAIN RULE: every fact these screens show was written by US-34 and US-35, the only new port method is an aggregate for the overview, and the only edit to src/domain/ is the DistributionSessionNotFound code in story 2 — a typed error, not a rule. A story that finds itself editing prisma/, or writing anything in src/domain/ that decides an outcome, has misread the batch. NO NEW ADR either — ADR-020 and ADR-021 already carry the decisions this screen renders. Story 5's e2e spec is THE ONLY END-TO-END PROOF THAT US-35 DID ANYTHING AT ALL: serve, end, rename the household, and watch the old name still stand. Requirements: local_only/manually-start-ausgabe/refined-requirements.md requirements C and E-1…E-4, E-6. Full PRD: tasks/prd-us-37-session-overview-and-detail.md

userStories.title: The list of sessions (application)
userStories.description: As DF, I want one call to answer what every past afternoon did, so the overview is one query rather than one per row. Source: tasks/prd-us-37-session-overview-and-detail.md §US-37.1
acceptanceCriteria: NEW use case src/application/distribution/list-distribution-sessions.ts returning, NEWEST FIRST, one row per session that was NOT discarded: { id, startedAt, endedAt, groups, households, totalPaidCents, running }

households and totalPaidCents are AGGREGATED IN THE STORE, not by loading every hand-out of every session: a NEW port method DistributionRecordRepository.summariseBySession() returning a map, in the shape CardRepository.highestIndexByNumber already takes. ONE QUERY for the page, whatever the register's age
A RUNNING session is in the list, AT THE TOP, with running: true and PROVISIONAL figures. Its endedAt is null and THE SCREEN, not this use case, decides what to print there
Discarded sessions NEVER appear
Application coverage stays at 100%. Named tests: lists the newest session first / puts the running session at the top / counts what each session took / omits a discarded session
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: One new port method, an aggregate. A per-row query would be ~250 round trips after five years — the register's whole point is that it is small, not that it is slow.

userStories.title: One session, with the households that collected at it (application)
userStories.description: As DF, I want a session read back with its households as they stood, so the screen lays out an answer rather than assembling one. Source: tasks/prd-us-37-session-overview-and-detail.md §US-37.2
acceptanceCriteria: NEW use case src/application/distribution/read-distribution-session.ts taking a session id and returning the session plus ONE ROW PER HAND-OUT: { customerId, customerNumber, firstName, lastName, cardNumber, group, grownUps, children, priceCents, certificateValidUntil, reminderCount, paidCents, at }

WHICH STATE A ROW CARRIES IS DECIDED IN EXACTLY ONE PLACE, HERE: an ENDED session's rows come from the HandoutReceipt written when it closed (US-35); a RUNNING OR REOPENED session's rows are read LIVE off the customer, household, card and certificate. ONE if, with a comment naming the requirement and no more
IF THAT DECISION LEAKS INTO THE COMPONENT the screen will show frozen names in one column and live ones in another — the table nobody can check. It must not

group is groupOf(customerNumber) of WHICHEVER number the row carries (ADR-017), and cardNumber is formatCardNumber over WHICHEVER card slot and index it carries (ADR-016). NEITHER is stored, on the receipt or anywhere else
priceCents and paidCents come from the HAND-OUT, always — they are on it, frozen or not
THE HOUSEHOLD'S BALANCE IS NOT RETURNED: the difference on one row is readable from the two money columns, and the overall balance is a different question belonging to the household's own record
Rows are ordered by CUSTOMER NUMBER — the order DF read a register in — not by the time of the hand-out. One line on the use case says so

A session ended BEFORE US-35 has no receipts. Those rows come back with the household's LIVE values AND A FLAG SAYING SO, rather than empty columns the screen would have to guess at. One named test covers it

DistributionSessionNotFound for an unknown or discarded id. THE CODE DOES NOT EXIST YET and this is the ONE domain edit the batch makes: the union and the class in src/domain/errors.ts, and TIERS in src/app/notice-tier.ts, whose Record over the union FAILS THE BUILD until the code is tiered. A typed error is not a domain RULE. errors.test.ts covers it — domain coverage is gated at 100%

Application coverage stays at 100%. Named tests: shows the name as it stood at an ended session / shows today's name while the session is still running / shows today's name again after the session is reopened / shows the household that was served after its number was given to another
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: This is the story the whole of US-35 was built for. The single most important line in it is the one that decides receipt-or-live, and it belongs here and nowhere else.

userStories.title: The overview page (presentation)
userStories.description: As DF, I want a page listing the distributions we have held, so that last Thursday is one click away. Source: tasks/prd-us-37-session-overview-and-detail.md §US-37.3
acceptanceCriteria: NEW route /ausgabetermine — DF's own word, and DELIBERATELY NOT /ausgaben, which is one letter from the counter screen /ausgabe and would be misread in the address bar and in every future conversation about the code

ONE TABLE, newest first: Datum, Gruppe(n), Haushalte, Summe. The RUNNING session is the first row and is MARKED as running — a badge, not a colour alone (ui_styling_guide.md §12) — with its figures labelled provisional in ONE WORD, not a sentence
Group(s) wear the SAME BADGE as everywhere else in the application (GROUP_STYLES, variant="outline"); a session serving both shows both badges
Each row links to the detail view. Money is formatted through src/domain/money.ts; dates through src/i18n/format.ts
An EMPTY register says so in ONE LINE and nothing more — no explanation of what will appear here once DF have held a distribution

Reached from /ausgabe: the last session's summary links here, and so does the session header while one runs. WHETHER A FIFTH NAV ITEM IS ADDED IS DECIDED ON THE FINISHED SCREEN — the nav bar is the application's only wayfinding and four items is what US-17 settled on, so adding one is a decision with a cost, not a detail

German strings ONLY in src/i18n/de.ts, under distribution.pastSessions — NOT distribution.sessions, which is ONE LETTER from the distribution.session US-34 wrote for the afternoon under way. Two keys in one object telling singular from plural is the misreading /ausgabetermine was chosen over /ausgaben to avoid
Wide content scrolls inside its own container; the page body never scrolls horizontally
Verify in the browser with the playwright-cli skill — the ACCESSIBILITY SNAPSHOT is what shows whether nine columns still mean anything
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: A read-only screen and the first one in the application that is not about today. Keep it boring: a table, newest first, one badge, one link.

userStories.title: The detail view (presentation)
userStories.description: As DF, I want to open one distribution and see who collected and what they paid, so that a question about last Thursday is answered from the screen rather than from memory. Source: tasks/prd-us-37-session-overview-and-detail.md §US-37.4
acceptanceCriteria: NEW route /ausgabetermine/[id], HEADED by the session: the date, the start and end times, the group(s), the number of households and the total taken

ONE TABLE, one row per household that collected: Nr., Name, Karte, Gruppe, Erw. + Kinder, Preis, Nachweis bis, Erinnerungen, Betrag. Headings are THE CUSTOMER LIST'S OWN, read from the same de.ts keys where they are the same words — a second wording of one column is how two screens come to disagree
NO Status COLUMN: whoever appears in the table was active at the time of their hand-out anyway, a blocked household receiving nothing
NO LIST OF ABSENT HOUSEHOLDS and NO LIST OF BLOCKS OR ARCHIVINGS — this is a deliberate decision of DF's and supersedes the source specification's §3. NOTHING ON THE PAGE EXPLAINS THEIR ABSENCE

THE WIDTH IS DECIDED HERE, IN THE BROWSER, NOT ON PAPER. If nine columns do not read side by side at DF's window size, KARTE IS THE FIRST TO GO (a card number is made of the customer number and an issue count, so it partly repeats the first column). The table scrolls inside its own overflow-x container before the page ever scrolls sideways. Record the outcome in docs/guideline/ui_styling_guide.md if a column is dropped
A RUNNING or REOPENED session is viewable here like any other, its figures provisional, carrying the same one-word mark the overview uses. The page does NOT explain that numbers may still change

A session ended BEFORE US-35 shows its rows from the household's CURRENT record, marked in one short line — THE ONLY HINT ON THIS SCREEN THAT EARNS ITS PLACE, because it says something the table cannot: these figures are today's, not that afternoon's
An ended session with NO hand-outs says so in one line
NOTHING on this screen is editable: a past session is read-only, and a running one is corrected at the counter where it is being served
Verify in the browser with the playwright-cli skill — the ACCESSIBILITY SNAPSHOT is what shows whether nine columns still mean anything
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: Nine columns is the risk. The customer list already has width trouble with eight of them and this project capped a column on that list once already (PR #141). Judge it at DF's window size, on a MacBook, and drop Karte if something must go.

userStories.title: The state as it stood, proved end to end (e2e)
userStories.description: As a developer, I want the freeze proved through the screen, because the capture built in US-35 has never been read by anything until now. Source: tasks/prd-us-37-session-overview-and-detail.md §US-37.5
acceptanceCriteria: NEW tests/e2e/session-detail.spec.ts: start a session, serve two households, open the detail view WHILE IT RUNS and see them with today's values
End it; the figures are unchanged
THEN CHANGE THE HOUSEHOLD: correct the surname, renew the certificate, re-open the detail view — THE OLD SURNAME AND THE OLD DATE STILL STAND
Reopen the session: the detail view FOLLOWS THE RECORD AGAIN
End it once more: the detail view freezes on the NEW values, because the afternoon was closed a second time
Archive one household's number and register a new household on it, then re-open the past session — THE ROW STILL NAMES THE HOUSEHOLD THAT WAS ACTUALLY SERVED
The overview lists the sessions newest first and marks the running one
BOTH ENGINES PASS: npm run test:e2e and npm run test:e2e:webkit. Stop any running dev server first
Full unit suite passes with coverage: npm run test:coverage
Typecheck passes
Lint passes
userStories.notes: This spec is the only end-to-end proof that US-35 did anything at all. Use the session helper from tests/e2e/session.ts and its own register slice — it archives a number, so it must not share numbers with another spec.
